q1_issues.issue: 'simple majority' is a term of art (a named voting threshold), so the adjective+noun pair should fuse to simple_majority plus its genus atom; the split form instead predicates the property 'simple' of the majority, which is the incidental-description treatment the fusion rule reserves for colour/size/damage/mood.

Patient on the vote overreads the occurrence-object carve-out, which covers only verbs that change whether or when an occurrence happens (cancel / postpone / reschedule); 'decide' settles its outcome, so the unclear-case default Theme applies.

notes: The specific-witness (non-generic) reading is what the instruction set mandates for an indefinite subject with a verbal predicate, even though the sentence reads as a standing procedural rule, and the absent status atom is the correct habitual default. The singular collective 'majority' correctly gets a plain witness with no GroupOf and no distribution rule.
